About **82% of revenue is online and 18% is offline**, out of ₹1,060.8 Cr total across all time.

| Group | Channels | Revenue (₹) | Share |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Online** | PLATFORM, D2C, QCOMM, INTERNATIONAL | 8,659,335,100 | **81.6%** |
| **Offline** | OFFLINE (retail), CAFE | 1,948,676,591 | **18.4%** |
| Total | | 10,608,011,691 | 100% |

**By channel:**

| Channel | Revenue (₹ Cr) | Share |
|---|---|---|
| PLATFORM | 309.1 | 29.1% |
| D2C | 238.6 | 22.5% |
| QCOMM | 200.2 | 18.9% |
| OFFLINE | 124.0 | 11.7% |
| INTERNATIONAL | 118.1 | 11.1% |
| CAFE | 70.8 | 6.7% |

**How I grouped the channels:** The data doesn't label channels as online or offline. The column descriptions mention a `dim_channels` table with a channel group, but it doesn't exist in `dev_dna_silver`. So I treated CAFE as offline because it's in-store sales. I put INTERNATIONAL with online because those orders have shipping and customs. If "offline" should mean only the OFFLINE retail channel, the split is **88.3% online and 11.7% offline**.

**How it was calculated:**
- **Source:** the `sales` semantic-layer source, using `sales.revenue_inr` grouped by `sales.channel_code`.
- **Revenue definition:** the standard company one. It covers all dates and all order statuses, and excludes soft-deleted rows.
- **International revenue:** converted from USD at a fixed 83 INR/USD.
- **Check:** the online and offline totals add up to the overall total.

I didn't save the online/offline grouping to ktx memory because it's my assumption. If you confirm how channels should be grouped, I can save it so future questions use it automatically.
